  reappears while opening the module in HR"). Pulled web first (ff to teammate's post-sales work, clean). TWO
  root causes, both fixed: (1) components/ui/map-view.tsx — `colorScheme` is a Google Maps CONSTRUCTION option;
  @vis.gl/react-google-maps destroys+recreates the whole map when it changes. `isDark` was initialized to false
  then flipped in a mount effect, so in dark mode every open did LIGHT→DARK → map recreated → blank→reload. Fix:
  lazy-init isDark synchronously from document.documentElement.classList (SSR-guarded) so colorScheme is stable
  from first render; the observer effect still handles live theme toggles. (2) app/geotrack/live/page.tsx —
  `formattedDisplayDate` useMemo sat AFTER the `if (permissionsLoading) return <skeleton>` early return (rules-of-
  hooks violation). When permissions finish loading (true→false, exactly as the module opens) the hook count
  changed → React "rendered more hooks than previous render" → error-boundary remount of the subtree → whole page
  incl. map blanks+reappears. Fix: moved the useMemo above the early return; verified no other hooks remain after
  it. Visual before/after not reproduced here (geotrack page needs a logged-in portal session + Maps key + live
  convex data — same auth blocker as the app OTP). tsc scoped check running. No Convex change; no deploy.

- 2026-08-19 (main-chat) — WEB (max): fixed device-binding bypass — a 2nd phone (old-build Oppo) could log into an
  account already locked to another device (emulator), and the binding kept showing the emulator. ROOT CAUSE: the
  login gate keyed on deviceId PRESENCE (`if (args.deviceId?.trim())`), so any client that sends no deviceId (older
  app build) skipped enforcement entirely = free bypass. Analyzed full chain (http.ts routes forward deviceId;
  verifyOtp/loginWithEmployeeId call enforceMobileDeviceBinding pre-session; block is real). FIX (3 files, tsc clean
  in my files): (1) convex/staffDeviceBinding.ts enforceMobileDeviceBinding — grace path now survives ONLY when NO
  binding exists yet; once bound, a mobile login with a MISSING or mismatched id is blocked (was: missing id →
  grace-allow). (2+3) authFunctions.ts verifyOtp + passwordAuth.ts loginWithEmployeeId — gate changed from
  `if (args.deviceId?.trim())` to `if (deviceType === "mobile")`, pass `deviceId: args.deviceId ?? ""`. Safe because
  resolveAuthDeviceType FORCES "web" for any non-native UA (browser can't spoof mobile) → web/PC stays unlocked.
  NO mass-lockout risk: a binding is only ever created by a build that sends an id (old builds send none at login
  AND push-register), so every bound account's real device re-sends a matching id and is never blocked; and it's
  login-only (never deactivates a session). Recovery for current state: admin "Reset Device" (clears lock +
  deactivateMobileSessionsForStaff) then log in from the intended device on the NEW build. NEEDS CONVEX DEPLOY to
  take effect on prod (mg.theairix.com). Pushed max 7495444f. No app change required for the block to work.

- 2026-08-22 (main-chat) — APP-WIDE OFFLINE DATA ("opened app online, turned network off, all loaded data gone,
  no cache"). INVESTIGATION: first disproved the scary hypothesis — nothing WIPES the cache offline (the 401
  authWatchdog only fires on a real HTTP 401; offline throws IOException; session.clearSession() doesn't touch
  LocalCache; only LogoutBottomSheet/ForcePasswordChange call clearAll). REAL CAUSE: only 6 screens ever cached
  (HomeFragment, HrDashboard, AttendanceHistory, AttendanceFlowVM, ChatList, ChatMessages, TaskManager) — 30+
  others (Leaves, Permissions, Collections, Fines, CP/SV visits, Loans, Bookings, DailyLog, Notifications, Fleet,
  Land, PostSales…) had NO cache, so any resume/navigation re-fetch threw and rendered blank. FIX (merge
  583dc7b5, compile GREEN, 19/19 tests): NEW network/OfflineHttpCache.kt — shared 40MB OkHttp disk Cache wired
  into ALL THREE singleton clients (ApiService, GeoTrackApi, DailyLogApi) + MconnectAppContext (set in
  MconnectApp.onCreate before any client builds). storeResponses (network interceptor): backend sends NO cache
  headers so nothing was storable — tags successful GETs `max-age=0` (stored but instantly stale ⇒ ONLINE
  behaviour byte-identical, always hits network) + `Vary: Authorization` (a cached entry is only replayed for the
  SAME bearer token ⇒ no cross-user leak); skips /api/auth/* and /api/storage/upload. serveStaleWhenOffline (app
  interceptor): FAILURE-DRIVEN — proceeds normally and only on IOException retries with onlyIfCached+maxStale 30d;
  cache miss RETHROWS the original IOException so screens behave exactly as before. DESIGN NOTE: deliberately
  rejected my first draft that gated on ConnectivityManager NET_CAPABILITY_VALIDATED — that can read false while
  the network works (captive portal / validation pending) and would serve STALE data to an ONLINE user. Writes
  (POST/PUT/DELETE) are never cached ⇒ punch/collection/loan mutations keep their existing offline queues
  untouched. LogoutBottomSheet now also calls OfflineHttpCache.clear(). NOT VERIFIED E2E: emulator was wedged
  (offline state) and data screens need an OTP login I can't perform — needs a device pass: load screens online,
  enable airplane mode, navigate back to each screen, confirm data renders (and that a fresh login still fetches
  live data). Needs new APK.

  already found. SYMPTOM MAPPING CONFIRMED IN CODE: AttendanceHistoryFragment does
  `runCatching{ getAllAttendance }.getOrNull()` then `fillAbsentDays(...)` — a FAILED fetch is swallowed and
  every dateless day is synthesised as "Absent". So a 500 from the backend renders as the whole company being
  absent. That is why it looks offline while online. TWO FIXES: (1) APP RESILIENCE — OfflineHttpCache now
  replays the last-known GET on 5xx, not only on IOException; a failing backend empties a screen exactly like
  no-network does. Strictly 5xx: 401/403/404 still reach the caller (auth watchdog + real empty states).
  GOTCHA FOUND BY TEST: the replay silently never worked because OkHttp refuses a new request while the
  previous response body is open — "cannot make a new request because the previous response is still open".
  Must drain+close the error body BEFORE calling the cache, then rebuild the response if the cache misses.
  Proved with a throwaway probe test that printed the actual IllegalStateException rather than guessing.
  (2) ROOT CAUSE — /api/hr/attendance/all now uses listForReportPaginated (200/page, cursor) instead of one
  capped read. The old cap did BOTH bad things: enrichment over thousands of rows blew the read budget so the
  request failed, and whatever came back was truncated — and a truncated day is an "Absent" day. Response
  keeps `records` and adds nextCursor/hasMore, so older builds still render page one. Android All tab pages
  via InfiniteScrollPager.onEndReached with id-dedup; cursor cleared when the date range changes.

## 2026-08-27/28 — offline attendance, and four real defects in it

The pipeline already existed (queue with the real tap time, WorkManager replay,
backend honouring the device timestamp). Four things were broken:

1. The selfie was stored RAW — compression only ran on the online upload path,
   so the offline branch queued a multi-MB original that then had to replay over
   a weak connection. Compression moved into OfflinePunchQueue.enqueue, the
   chokepoint.
2. HomeViewModel had a private COPY of the queue logic — the drift the shared
   helper's own doc says it exists to prevent, and it had already drifted (raw
   selfie, always-null address). Now calls the shared queue, and the
   reverse-geocoded address is resolved before the try so the offline branch
   carries it.
3. A punch older than 24h silently lost its real time: the backend rewrote it to
   the SYNC time, so a Monday 9am clock-in synced Wednesday landed as Wednesday.
   Second-order effect — the replay then looked live and lost the no-GPS
   exemption, so it could be rejected outright. Window widened to 7 days, moved
   into lib/attendanceTime.ts with serverNow injectable.
4. A queued punch was not bound to its staff, so it could replay under whoever
   signed in next. PendingPunchEntity now carries staffId (Room v6, additive
   ALTER); pre-upgrade rows carry null and still flush.

## 2026-08-28 — two client-side bugs found by tracing, not guessing

Home said "Clock In First" while Attendance said clocked in. Home derives the
gate from two calls that swallow failure to null, then wrote hasOpenSession =
FALSE — so one flaky refresh silently downgraded a clocked-in staff member and
locked every trip. Now: if the summary call fails but sessions answers, derive
from sessions; if neither answers, KEEP the previous values. Clock-out is
unaffected because that path returns a real "no open session" response — only
silence stopped being treated as "no". Verified pre-existing: my only prior
commit in that file changed punch() alone.

A completed CP showed "Enroute" with a Start action forever. The card's status
preferred the FIELD VISIT, which is right while a trip is live (only it tracks
"arrived") but wrong once the CP is finished: the app closes the field visit in a
SECOND call, and when that fails the CP is completed server-side while its trip
row is stuck in-progress. A terminal CP status now wins. Fixed in ONE shared
helper because the two screens had drifted — CP Visits honoured
pending_gm_approval but not completion; Home honoured neither.

## 2026-08-28 — collection timestamps showed UTC, not local time

Reported as "showing 5 am". 05:35 + 5:30 = 11:05 — exactly the IST offset.

The server stores createdAt as new Date().toISOString(), a UTC instant. The
Android parser's Z is QUOTED in the pattern, so it matches the LETTER Z rather
than meaning UTC, and with no timeZone set SimpleDateFormat parses in the
device's zone. The UTC wall clock was read as if it were already local.

Parsers now read UTC; the display formatter stays local. dateOnlyFormat is
deliberately left local — a bare yyyy-MM-dd is a calendar date, not an instant.
Same defect fixed in LoanData. The two attendance sheets already set UTC
correctly, so the right pattern was already in the codebase.

It also shifted DATES, not just times: anything after 18:30 IST falls on the
previous UTC day, so an evening collection could show yesterday. Display-only —
the stored data was always correct, so it fixes retroactively.

## 2026-08-28 — "client not met" follow-up rewritten

Both reported problems had one cause: the 48h cron PATCHED the closed visit back
to "scheduled" and cleared its outcome, completedAt and clientMet.

- "the closed CP is not showing" — the only record of the close was the row it
  had just overwritten, so the failed attempt disappeared.
- "the follow-up date is not appropriate" — the reactivated row carried the
  ORIGINAL visit's identity, and its date came from whenever the cron swept.

Now it creates a NEW visit and leaves the closed one closed. The retry is
anchored on the CLOSE (lastNotMetAt + 48h), not on "now", and is never dated in
the past — a backlog close would otherwise produce a visit created already
overdue, so those land today. The original is stamped handled even when the spawn
is refused, because retrying a rejected spawn hourly would just repeat the
failure. Each retry is a normal CP, so missing it again closes THAT row and
spawns the next — a visible chain instead of one row rewritten repeatedly.

Only affects FUTURE closes; CPs already erased by the old behaviour cannot be
recovered.

## 2026-08-29 - CP approval travelled path and card UI

- Investigated the CP approval trip dialog after it showed a straight start/end line with “full GPS trail unavailable”.
- Confirmed Android and iOS both call `/api/marketing/cp-visits/approval-route` and intentionally fall back to connecting endpoint coordinates.

## 2026-08-29 - Missing CP travelled distance on pending approval
- Investigated the reported `Distance travelled: Not recorded` approval card. The native formatter is receiving `null`; this is not a display-formatting issue.
- Found a lifecycle/data-ownership gap: `setOutcome` creates the `pending_gm_approval` row before Android calls `completeVisit`; `completeVisit` later calculates the GPS trail distance but stores it only on the linked trip/tracking session. The approval queue therefore depends on transient linkage and can return no distance during timing races or for records whose trip/session link is incomplete.
- Implementing a backend-owned distance snapshot on `completionApproval` when the field visit finalizes. Approval reads will prefer that stable value and retain linked session/trip fallbacks for existing data. Shared backend behavior means Android, web, and iOS receive the fix without separate client changes.
- Added `completionApproval.travelledDistanceMeters` to the Convex schema, copied the finalized GPS trail distance there in `hr.fieldVisits.completeVisit`, and updated approval reads to prefer the stable snapshot before linked tracking-session/GeoTrip fallbacks.
- Added regression coverage for both the real mobile ordering (pending approval first, trip completion second) and historical approvals that only have linked-trip distance. Focused CP approval tests pass 11/11, full `npx tsc --noEmit` passes, and diff hygiene passes (line-ending warnings only).
- Confirmed the release topology: pushes to `max` run CI/build checks only; production Convex deployment is explicitly local via `deploy.sh --convex-only`. Therefore the earlier pushed client/UI field can render while production still omits the backend value, producing the reported `Not recorded`. The new backend fix is prepared but has not been committed, pushed, or deployed in this turn; production deployment requires an explicit release decision.

## 2026-09-02 - Safe deferred Android auto-update investigation (in progress)
- User requested background app updates that never interrupt tracking or any active CP/SV/workflow, install only while operationally idle, and otherwise prompt for an app restart. Began auditing the current distribution/update implementation, manifest privileges, GeoTrack lifecycle, and reliable active-work signals before deciding whether Android platform restrictions permit the requested behavior without operational risk.
- Found an existing Google Play in-app updater already committed in the Android app. Its old policy could launch an immediate blocking update solely from Play release priority and could offer/restart updates without checking attendance, GeoTrack, field work, calls, or offline queues, so it did not satisfy the requested operational safety requirement.
- Reworked the updater to use new flexible updates only and added a fail-closed `OperationalUpdateGate`. It postpones every update action while tracking is requested/active, an attendance session is open or cannot be verified, a CP/SV/fleet/on-duty activity is persisted, a Modern Dialer call/notification is active, or location/tracking-event/punch/chat data remains queued locally. External fleet users use their persisted fleet-activity state because staff attendance endpoints do not apply to them.
- Restricted update prompts and background installation to the idle Home root with no navigation back stack or visible dialog. A downloaded update completes through Google Play only after `MainActivity` is stopped and a second safety check passes; if it remains downloaded when the app next opens safely, the app shows `App restart needed to install new updates`. Foreground/background state is rechecked after asynchronous safety calls to avoid a delayed background callback restarting an app the user has already reopened.
- Added focused policy tests proving the fully idle state is allowed and every tracked operational/unknown/queued signal blocks installation. The focused test plus `:app:assembleDebug` passed. Full regression tests and final diff validation are still pending. No web/backend/iOS source or API contract was changed.

No new backend API is required for the conservative gate because it reuses the existing attendance endpoints plus persisted operational state and Room queues.

## 2026-09-03 - Prevent tracking before first clock-in (in progress)

- User reported that a staff timeline contains mobile tracking/network/location events before the staff's first 9:36 AM punch and requested a mobile fix plus any required API additions to the consolidated outstanding handoff. Beginning a fail-closed audit of Android boot/app/service start paths, attendance-session validation, persisted tracking state, and iOS parity. No product source, API contract, production data, Git ref, commit, push, or deployment has changed at this checkpoint.
- Root cause confirmed on Android: `GeoTrackService` registered location/activity/network receivers and started tamper plus heartbeat loops before its asynchronous attendance check completed; `BootReceiver` also trusted stale persisted tracking state and queued reboot/update timeline evidence before attendance reconciliation. iOS had the equivalent cold-launch risk by reusing yesterday's persisted `shouldTrackNow` whenever attendance APIs were unavailable.
- Android now fail-closes every cold bootstrap/service start until `attendance/today` or `attendance/day-sessions` authoritatively confirms an open punch session. The service enters Android's required foreground state but initializes no GPS, activity recognition, heartbeat, network callback, permission event, tamper event, or last-location update until that confirmation. A verified running shift still continues through an unknown/transient attendance response, and an authoritative false stops and clears stale tracking state. Boot/update events are queued only after the same gate succeeds.
- iOS now reuses persisted tracking state on an unknown attendance response only when its `LocationTracker` is already verified and running in the current process. A cold launch with unknown/false attendance cannot start Core Location, heartbeat, tamper, activity, or upload loops.
- Added focused Android policy tests for cold-start fail-closed and verified-running outage behavior. Initial Gradle invocation failed only because `JAVA_HOME` was absent; reran with Android Studio JBR. Full `:app:testDebugUnitTest :app:assembleDebug` passed (`BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, 48 tasks).
- Extended `reports/MOBILE_OUTSTANDING_API_REQUIREMENTS.md` with a P0 Attendance-Bounded GeoTrack section covering existing attendance/bootstrap/device/location/heartbeat/tamper endpoints, required timestamp-window validation, stale-session behavior, non-retryable `OUTSIDE_ATTENDANCE_WINDOW`, batch rejection semantics, and seven release acceptance checks. No new route is requested.
- Added a historical-repair requirement to dry-run and then remove/quarantine already persisted events outside each canonical punch interval, recomputing derived live status, distance, movement, battery, offline, and tamper summaries without changing attendance or valid CP/SV records. ## 2026-09-05 - Same-phone reinstall device-binding investigation (backend/distribution diagnosis)

- User reported a staff member being rejected as bound to another device after uninstalling and reinstalling on the claimed same phone. Audited Android/iOS login identifiers, persistence, signing sensitivity, fresh-install session cleanup and existing device-reset APIs.
- Android login already sends `Settings.Secure.ANDROID_ID`, which survives ordinary uninstall/reinstall for the same device, Android user and app-signing certificate but changes when the app-signing certificate changes (for example, switching between Play Store and a differently signed sideloaded APK), after factory reset or under another Android user/profile. Android's separate tracking UUID is not used for login binding.
- iOS current code stores its binding UUID in a `ThisDeviceOnly` Keychain item, which survives reinstall and does not migrate to another phone. A backend mismatch can still affect a user whose binding was created by an older identifierForVendor-only build and who uninstalled before the Keychain migration was installed, or when signing/Keychain access identity changed.
- The backend compares one opaque device ID. Mobile cannot safely prove physical-device sameness after that ID changes; accepting platform/model alone would allow another identical phone to bypass the single-device lock. Existing authorized recovery is `POST /api/hr/staff/device-reset`, after which the official consistently signed app can bind again. Exact root cause for this staff member requires platform and install-source/version information plus comparison of the stored/current binding IDs in backend logs.

- Began replacing misleading `Recover/reset another device` presentation with `Verify this device`. Internal endpoint/state names remain unchanged to preserve the established backend contract.
- Did not add MAC, IMEI, serial-number or model-based matching. Official Android guidance states ordinary apps cannot access hardware MAC addresses and network MACs are randomized; `ANDROID_ID` is scoped to signing key, user and device and can change after factory reset or signing-key changes. Official Apple guidance states `identifierForVendor` can change after all vendor apps are removed/reinstalled or with some test/ad-hoc installations. The existing iOS Keychain identifier reduces that reinstall gap; neither value is proof of genuine hardware by itself.

- 2026-09-12: Audited the GeoTrack/Convex split after the user flagged tracking traffic still hitting `api-mfpl.theairix.com`, and produced a backend handoff spec at `reports/GEOTRACK_CONVEX_CUTOVER.md`; no web/Convex file was edited and no app code changed this turn. Three findings. The flagged paths (`/api/geotrack/tamper/report` 16.36k, `/api/tracking/bootstrap` 4.28k, `/api/tracking/device/sync` 4.26k, `/api/tracking/heartbeat` 404) are called by NOTHING in the current Android app, iOS app or web — they were removed by commit `e54016d7` (2026-09-09, versionCode 72, "use direct tracking service"), so the traffic is phones still on versionCode <= 71 and decays with a minimum-version bump through the existing `/api/mobile/app-version` gate. Far more serious, that same migration starved Convex's `locationPoints` table while leaving every consumer of it in place: `geotrack/trips.ts:609` (`completeOnDutyTrip`), `trips.ts:329`, `travelAllowance.ts:505`, `marketing/clientPlaceVisits.ts:677/983/1224/10788`, `hr/fieldVisits.ts:1016`, `geotrack/monitoring.ts:268`, `geotrack/roads.ts:201/337` and `adminCpVisitRepair.ts:2139` all still scan it, so on-duty and CP distances now sum to zero and fall back to a straight line start-to-end — a staff member who drives a 40 km loop and returns near the start records about 0 m, drops under the >1 km travel-allowance qualifier and is silently unpaid, with no error logged. The blocker on fixing that cleanly is the third finding: the app only ever starts a session with `contextType="attendance"` and `contextId=attendanceId` (`HomeViewModel.kt:328`, `AttendanceFlowViewModel.kt:450`, `PunchSyncWorker.kt:101`), so CP trips and on-duty trips are never linked to the session and the geo service cannot attribute points to them. The spec therefore asks for two endpoint groups on `api-geo`: telemetry read-back (`/api/tracking/metrics/distance`, `/metrics/batch`, `/metrics/path`, `/points/latest`) so Convex stops reading a dead table, and a segment model (`/api/tracking/segments/start|end|reconcile`, plus a GET) where one attendance-day session carries CP-trip/on-duty segments and `segments/end` returns the authoritative distance in its response. Both groups are called from Convex, deliberately, so already-installed phones are fixed without an app release. The spec also states explicitly which eight Convex routes must NOT be migrated (`assigned-places`, `today-visits`, `visit/create|start|complete`, `visit/arrival-otp/*`, `on-duty/start|complete`) because they mutate business records and moving them would break working modules, and carries an appendix repeating the two CP arrival-OTP reveal routes from earlier today so the same admin gets one file. `AGENT_LOG.md` remains local-only.
- 2026-09-12: Implemented the app-side GeoTrack context linkage on BOTH platforms and updated `reports/GEOTRACK_CONVEX_CUTOVER.md` to match; still no web/Convex edit. Every location point and heartbeat now carries `contextType` (`attendance`/`cp_trip`/`site_visit`/`on_duty`/`fleet_trip`) and `contextId` (the Convex trip row id), which is what lets the GeoTrack service attribute distance to a trip instead of guessing from a time window. Both platforms stamp the context at CAPTURE time, never at flush: a backlog uploaded hours later keeps the trip it was recorded during, the same rule the existing `sessionId` column already follows, and the flush path copies the buffered row's values rather than re-reading the live store. No extra tracking session is created for a trip — that would violate the standing clock-in-to-clock-out tracking window and tear the point stream — so a trip is a stretch of the day's session. Android: new `geotrack/TrackingContext.kt`, `FieldActivity` gained `refId` with `setFieldActivity(refId=)` and a new `updateFieldActivityRef(kind, refId)` for on-duty (which sets the activity before it knows its `geoTrips._id`, so the id is attached when the start call answers and the whole trip is attributed), Room `pending_points` gained `contextType`/`contextId` via additive `MIGRATION_6_7` at version 7, and the queued-heartbeat replay carries the snapshot's context rather than re-reading the session. iOS: new `Services/GeoTrackTrackingContext.swift` mirroring the same kinds and strings (iOS has no tracking notification, so the store is standalone and UserDefaults-backed, with a fallback read of the pre-existing `attendance.onDuty.tripId` key so an on-duty trip started on an older build still attributes), Core Data gained the two optional attributes scoped under the existing `includeTrackingContext` flag so `makeModel(includeTrackingContext: false)` keeps describing the ORIGINAL on-disk schema that the legacy migration uses as its source, and trip lifecycle wired at CP/SV start, fleet driver start, all three `completeVisit` sites, on-duty start/complete and punch-out. Two ordering corrections during the iOS work: a bulk replace clobbered `let completion = try await geoAPI.completeVisit(` and broke an if-block's indentation, and the clears were initially placed BEFORE completion — moved after, matching Android, so a completion that throws leaves the trip open and its points keep the trip's tag. Also added `endTripContext()` which clears only the cp/sv/fleet kinds, because a staff member can be on duty for the day AND run a CP trip inside it. Parity audit confirmed iOS already has the HR Security screen with active-logins and logout-everywhere, CP approvals, joint CP and OTP assist, plus this session's OTP reveal. Android: 292 tests with zero failures/errors (7 new `TrackingContextTest` cases), `:app:assembleDebug` passed, and `:app:compileDebugKotlin --rerun-tasks` forced a full recompile. iOS remains source-verified only (brace/paren balance clean on all seven touched files); it needs a Mac build. No backend/prod data, deployment, commit or push occurred.

- 2026-09-12: User reported "geo tracking is not working" and pointed at the geo-tracking-service repo (branch `kira`, present locally, a Go service). Diagnosed two gaps by diffing every direct-GeoTrack URL the app calls against the service's registered routes. Gap 1: `/api/geotrack/session-route` has NO handler — the only one of fifteen missing — so `GeoTrackLiveFragment` and `AttendanceReviewBottomSheet` both 404, which is the visible "tracking shows nothing". Gap 2, larger: Go marshals `time.Time` as RFC 3339 and names keys `tripId`/`sessionId`/`state`, while the published mobile contract is epoch millis with `_id`/`sessionState`; Gson cannot read an RFC 3339 string into a `Long`, so it threw and discarded the ENTIRE payload, silently. Fixed the half I could verify: new `network/EpochMillisAdapter.kt` accepts a number, a numeric string or RFC 3339, normalizes Go's variable-length fractional seconds, and keeps a `+05:30` offset at its true instant rather than reading it as UTC (the same class of defect as the collection 5:30 bug); applied per field via `@JsonAdapter` rather than globally so the leniency covers only the timestamps crossing this boundary, plus `SerializedName` alternates for `_id`/`tripId`/`sessionId` and `sessionState`/`state`. Nine regression tests; full Android suite 301 tests with zero failures/errors and `:app:assembleDebug` passed. Did NOT write Go: no toolchain exists anywhere on this machine and `AGENTS.md` requires `make check` before committing, so unverifiable Go was not pushed to the service carrying live attendance tracking; instead committed `docs/MOBILE_CONTRACT_GAPS.md` to `kira` with the full session-route contract, the mapping onto existing service methods (`Timeline`, `ListTrips`, `CurrentSession`, `GetTrip` cover every field, no new SQL), the seven-row mismatch table, and a recommendation to ADD compatible keys at the HTTP seam rather than rename so web consumers are untouched. Pulled Android from `main` (already an ancestor, no-op) and iOS from `darx` (fast-forward, a TestFlight build bump touching only project.pbxproj, no overlap with local edits) before pushing, as instructed. Second and more useful, the backend ALREADY answers the question — `notifications.listByUser` runs `resolveNotificationActionUrls`, so every notification carries an `actionUrl` like `/task-manager?taskId=…` or `/hr/salary-slips?month=8&year=2026` — but the app's `NotificationData` never declared the field, so Gson parsed it away and the information was discarded. Declared it nullable (per the standing Gson rule that one bad field kills the whole list parse) and added a three-step fallback: a mobile screen when one exists, otherwise the web deep link via the SAME `WebTaskLinkBottomSheet` the Task Manager already uses for web-only tasks so Open and Copy behave identically, and the old toast only when there is genuinely neither. The URL is composed from `BuildConfig.APP_URL` rather than a hardcoded host so a staging build links into staging, and absolute urls pass through untouched. Also mapped five types that do have mobile screens and were dead-ending: `siteVisit` (an alias of the already-mapped `site-visit`), `issue`, `fine-deduction`, `customerCollection`, and `geo-trip`/`geotrack-tamper`. The IAM gate is untouched and still evaluated first, so nothing can route a user into a screen they lack access to. Note the screenshot's own case, `dailyTask`, was already mapped — so that particular tap was either IAM-gated or a neighbouring notification; the fix addresses the whole class either way. 315 tests, zero failures; `:app:assembleDebug` clean. Android only — the iOS notification list has its own routing and was not in scope this turn.
- 2026-09-15: Diagnosed the web GeoTrack Live failure ("Live tracking is temporarily unavailable" with `{"success":false,"error":"Geo tracking service returned invalid JSON"}`). Answer to the user's question: it is NEITHER mobile nor web app code — the string comes from `convex/lib/geoTrackingService.ts:86`, where Convex `JSON.parse`s the geo service's response body. Probed the live service directly, read-only: `/healthz` returns `{"status":"ok"}` and `/readyz` reports postgres ok and redis ok, so the service is UP, and `/api/geotrack/live-status` and `/api/tracking/live` both return 200 with real staff rows — the data exists. But `/api/geotrack/stats`, `/api/geotrack/bootstrap`, `/api/tracking/bootstrap` and `/api/geotrack/session-route` all return **404 with `Content-Type: text/plain` and the body `404 page not found`**, Go's default `http.NotFound`. That plain-text body is exactly what breaks `JSON.parse`, producing the "invalid JSON" error verbatim. This is the §1.2 risk from `BACKEND_HANDOFF_2026-09-15.md` confirmed in production: the Convex proxy is forwarding to geo routes the Go service does not implement, and the zeroed Online/Offline/Geo-enabled tiles follow from the failing bootstrap/stats call rather than from any absence of data. SEPARATE AND MORE SERIOUS: every one of those probes was made with NO Authorization header and NO API key, from an unauthenticated shell, and `/api/geotrack/live-status`, `/api/tracking/live` and `/api/tracking/trips` all returned real staff ids, session data and trip geometry — 4.6 kB of trip records for a named staff id. Live staff location and movement history is therefore publicly readable on `api-geo.theairix.com`. This is consistent with the geo repo's own recent commits ("Allow auth-disabled deploy without API key", "Honor bearer tokens when geotrack auth is disabled"), which suggests the deployment is running with geotrack auth disabled. Flagged to the user as the priority item. No source, backend, deployment, commit or push change this turn.

- 2026-09-15: Fixed CP Visits crashing while scrolling (`fcfc3418`, pushed to `merge` and `main`). Could not pull a crash log — the OPPO was no longer attached, only an emulator — so diagnosed from the code. The list is a LinearLayout of inflated cards, not a RecyclerView, so every rebuilt row is a real `inflate()` on the main thread, and `rowViewCache` was an `IdentityHashMap` invalidated by `rowsBuiltFor !== allVisits`. Loading another page ALWAYS replaces `allVisits`, because the append does `(allVisits + incoming).distinctBy{}.sortedWith{}` — so each scroll-triggered fetch discarded every row already built and re-inflated the entire grown window, 20 cards then 40 then 60, on the main thread. That is the same failure mode as the previously-recorded Home visit-card ANR, and on a mid-range phone with a few hundred CPs it reads as a freeze then a death. Replaced with a HashMap keyed by the visit's stable id via a new `CpRowCachePolicy` (CP visit id, falling back to the field-visit id, with blank treated as absent), so a new page keeps every row it already built; reuse stays value-checked because `TodayVisit` is a data class, so a row whose data changed is still rebuilt and a completed visit redraws. Only the clock-in gate now clears everything, since that alters the action button on every row. Two hardening details: `addView` is preceded by detaching any lingering parent, because a view that still had one would throw `IllegalStateException` and take the screen down outright; and the cache is pruned each render to the keys the active filter can show, so it no longer accumulates a view for every row rendered in the session. An earlier hypothesis that duplicate `TodayVisit` values collided in the cache was wrong and discarded — the map was identity-keyed and the append already dedupes by `clientPlaceVisitId ?: id`. Eight tests on the reuse policy; full suite 323 tests with zero failures and `:app:assembleDebug` clean. Checked `SiteVisitsFragment` for the same pattern — it has no row cache, so it is unaffected. NOT reproduced on a device; the fix is reasoned and unit-tested only.
- 2026-09-15: Pulled the real crash from the OPPO's crash buffer and it was NOT the CP list. `java.lang.IllegalStateException: A migration from 7 to 6 was required but not found`, via `onDowngrade` -> `onUpgrade` — a Room DOWNGRADE, repeating at 09:26:50, 09:27:04 and 09:31:30 on background dispatchers. Cause is mine: the tracking-context work bumped `GeoTrackDatabase` to v7, the phone ran a v7 build and then went back to the Play build (versionCode 83, schema v6), and Room has no reverse migrations, so opening a v7 file with a v6 schema throws on EVERY database access and kills the process. Nothing to do with scrolling — it fires whenever anything touches the buffer, which the visit screens do constantly. Fixed with `fallbackToDestructiveMigrationOnDowngrade(dropAllTables = true)` (`78d72e1a`, pushed to `merge` and `main`): this database is a store-and-forward buffer whose points, events and punches are replayed to the backend, so dropping it on a downgrade is worth far more than a permanently crashing app, and it mirrors what the iOS GeoTrack Core Data store already does when its own migration fails. Upgrades are deliberately untouched so a genuinely missing upgrade path still fails loudly instead of silently wiping data. Confirmed `GeoTrackDatabase` is the app's only Room database, so no other builder needs the same guard. 323 tests, zero failures; `:app:assembleDebug` clean. Told the user plainly that the earlier `fcfc3418` row-cache change — which was reasoned from code without a crash log — was a genuine performance fix but NOT the cause of this crash, and that a phone already stuck in this state needs a v7-or-later build installed or its app storage cleared, since the guard only protects against the next downgrade.

Verified after launch: process alive (pid 17806), app resumed to `MainActivity` rather than `LoginActivity` so the session survived, crash buffer clean, and no "migration from 7 to 6" or any other Room error in logcat. The Room downgrade guard plus the v7 schema means the database now opens normally. Note the build still reports versionCode 83 because `app/build.gradle.kts` was not bumped — this is a branch build, not a Play release, so the number is unchanged from the previously installed one; that matters only if a Play update later needs to supersede it. - 2026-09-15: Verified on-device after the user scrolled CP Visits on the freshly installed build. Clean: same pid 17806 throughout so the process never restarted, crash buffer empty, no FATAL, no ANR, no `Choreographer ... Skipped frames` or `Davey` jank warnings, and no GC-pressure lines — which is the specific evidence the row-cache change in `fcfc3418` is doing its job, since the old behaviour re-inflated the whole grown window on the main thread on every scroll page and would have shown skipped frames. The Room downgrade crash is gone. One honest observation recorded rather than acted on: `dumpsys meminfo` reports **6173 Views** against 1 Activity and 1 ViewRootImpl, with Java heap 37 MB and TOTAL PSS 259 MB. That is expected for this screen's design — a LinearLayout that attaches every row in a window which grows 20 at a time as the user scrolls — and the cache fix removes the re-inflation cost but not the accumulation. It is stable at this list size; a genuinely long list will keep climbing, and the structural answer is a RecyclerView, which is a deliberate refactor rather than something to change reactively. Flagged to the user as a known limit, not a regression. The only app-side log lines during the session were benign `ChatListPhoto` debug output.
- 2026-09-15: Optimized the Security tab's logged-in-devices dialog (`3c08ae51`, pushed to `merge` and `main`, and installed on the OPPO). Each session was a stacked card — title, meta, then a full-width "Logout this device" block — at roughly 100dp per device, so three devices plus the dialog's own title and two-line message did not fit on a phone and the device list the admin opened the dialog to read was the part that scrolled off. Diagnosed two distinct causes and wrote `reports/GEOTRACK_LIVE_STILL_BROKEN_2026-09-15.md`; NO new endpoint is needed from anywhere. First, the merge is NOT deployed — probed `https://api-geo.theairix.com/api/geotrack/session-route?staffId=x&dayStart=1&dayEnd=2` and it still answers Go's default `404 page not found` as `text/plain`, whereas the merged `53b954f` would answer 400 for a bad `dayStart` and would serialize unknown paths as JSON; the running binary predates the commit, and a Git merge changes nothing until the service is rebuilt. - 2026-09-15: Diagnosed "Session could not be verified for this upload." on the trip screen and shipped a mitigation (`a18f4574`, pushed to `merge` and `main`). The string is `StorageUploader.kt:330`, a 401 from `mg.theairix.com/api/storage/uploads`. Could not pull the device evidence — the phone disconnected mid-dump and the backgrounded logcat returned only OS noise after the app's lines had rolled — so probed the endpoint directly instead: it is healthy, returning `{"success":false,"error":"unauthorized"}` with no auth and `{"success":false,"error":"invalid session"}` for a bogus bearer, both proper JSON. Root cause is in the web route's `requireStorageActor` (`lib/server/storage-auth.ts:38-42`), which validates the token by calling Convex `validateSession` with `.catch(() => null)` and then reports null as "invalid session" — so a slow, erroring or rate-limited Convex is indistinguishable from a genuinely bad session, and the user is told their login is broken when it is not. Compounding it, the uploader treated 404/503 as "try the compatibility endpoint" but every other 4xx as terminal, so a transient 401 killed the upload outright with no fallback. Changed 401 at the upload-CREATION stage to route to the same fallback via a named `isPreferredPathUnavailable`; deliberately left the PUT and completion stages terminal, because creation is the realistic failure point and falling back after the bytes are uploaded would re-send the whole file. The message now also names the stage, which it alone among the status codes omitted, so a future report can be traced to creation, upload or completion. Recorded plainly in the commit that this is a MITIGATION and the root fix belongs on the web side: storage-auth must distinguish "Convex said no" from "Convex did not answer". 323 tests, zero failures; `:app:assembleDebug` clean.

## 2026-09-18 — Prod: staff Offline while reporting; stale map position; stop after clock-out
- Prod measurement (unauth reads): 41 rows seen <=15min, 13 Offline. Group A (3): live row session != current active session → phone stamping an ENDED session; geo sets is_online from that session, so points refresh last_seen but force Offline. Group B (6): session offline_buffering (heartbeat-missed job) — points-only uploads never reset it. Group C (4): no active session yet still posting = tracking after clock-out.
- Far-away positions: outliers all had HEARTBEAT_MISSED (not mock) → stale last-known point drawn as if live.
- Mobile fix (GeoTrackService.verifyTrackingStillValid, every 10 min): re-check attendance (clock-out elsewhere → end + stop) and reconcile the session id (adopt server's active session, or re-open when clocked in and none). 346 tests pass, installed on phone + emulator (prod hosts).
- Wrote reports/GEOTRACK_OFFLINE_AND_STALE_POSITION_2026-09-18.md: geo should not let a late batch downgrade is_online, points path should clear offline_buffering like heartbeat does, review heartbeat-missed threshold, web should grey stale markers. Not committed/pushed.

## 2026-09-18 — Timeline mostly "Network Offline"
- Causes: (a) the web maps HEARTBEAT_MISSED/SILENT to "Network Offline"; (b) the geo service raises HEARTBEAT_MISSED after 5 min (Convex used 15 for Doze) and writes network_available=false with it; (c) app: the heartbeat `delay` stalled while the CPU slept, and hasNetwork() used activeNetwork (null when Doze blocks the app) and reported offline on a single network drop.
- App fix (GeoTrackService): wall-clock `awaitNextHeartbeat()` woken by an allow-while-idle alarm (ACTION_HEARTBEAT_TICK, 20s wakelock) or an overdue location fix; device-level network set; NETWORK_OFFLINE only after all networks are gone for 60s; NETWORK_ONLINE only after a reported outage. iOS doesn't emit these — no change.
- Verified on 77cd83cc: alarm registered, heartbeats 200. Backend/web asks: reports/GEOTRACK_TIMELINE_NO_NETWORK_2026-09-18.md. Not pushed.

## 2026-09-21 — Attendance approval panel anomaly (HARIKRISHNAN. M, 20 Sept)
- Diagnosed, no code changed. Root event: clocked in 09:24, never clocked out. The midnight finalizer closes such a session at its own punch-in instant (`convex/staffAttendance.ts:8024`, `autoClosedAtDayEnd`), so in==out and the day is Absent by design; the web summary tile renders that synthetic punch-out as real while the punch-log dialog already strips it.
- The 0 m / 0 trips / 0 points view of the same row is most likely a failed geo fetch: `useStaffDayGeo` empties the arrays and sets `error`, and the approvals panel never renders that error, so a failure looks like "no movement".
- Open mobile decision: with no clock-out, tracking + trip starts stay live until IST midnight (`AttendanceTrackingGate` / `scheduleAttendanceDayBoundaryStop`), which is why a 07:58 pm trip exists on an absent day.
- Written up in `reports/ATTENDANCE_APPROVAL_PANEL_2026-09-21.md` (web/Convex items are handoff only, per the no-edits rule).

## 2026-09-21 — Root cause found: geo panel shows the REVIEWER's own route
- Corrects the earlier entry today. Every per-staff geo read returns the CALLER's data: `requestStaffIdentifier` (geo `internal/httpapi/server.go:860`) overrides the requested `?staffId=` with the authenticated caller's id. Right for writes, wrong for the six admin read endpoints that share it. Introduced 2026-09-07 in geo commit `36f58a5`. `isWebReadPath` (security.go:219) already lists exactly those paths but is dead code.
- So the Vadapalani route/7:58 pm trip was Anand sir's, and the 0/0/0 view was the other reviewer's empty data — not a failed fetch as I first wrote. No cross-staff leak (a caller only ever sees themselves), but RO/HR decisions are made against the wrong person's map.
- Fix needs a viewer scope the geo service does not have (introspection returns only `{success, staffId}`). Two options written up; awaiting the user's choice before editing geo. No code changed.
- `reports/ATTENDANCE_APPROVAL_PANEL_2026-09-21.md` rewritten.

## 2026-09-21 — Geo fix pushed: per-staff reads no longer return the caller's rows
- geo-tracking-service `09c9710` on `dev` (auto-deploys dev-api-geo). `requestStaffIdentifier` now honours the requested `staffId` for a caller whose token carries viewer scope `all`, but only on the GET paths `isWebReadPath` lists (that function was dead code and is now wired). Writes stay pinned to the caller unconditionally.
- Scope comes from the token: introspection `scope: "all"` or `canViewAll: true`, or the same claims on a JWKS-verified JWT. Missing = `self` = today's behaviour, so the deploy is a no-op until Convex ships the field. Redis allow entries carry the scope; legacy `allow:<id>` entries read as `self`, no flush needed.

## 2026-09-23 — Joint CP "status was not finalized" fixed
- Symptom: saving a Not Interested outcome on a Joint CP showed "The outcome was received, but the CP status was not finalized." The save had actually succeeded.
- Root cause: `cpOutcomeConfirmationError` already skips the terminal-status check for a joint CP (the parent deliberately stays open until the reviewer completes it), but `isJointCp` was deciding jointness from the `cpType` argument alone. A Joint CP created through a category path carries that category (`booking_cp`, `sv_cum_cp`, `new_client_cp`) in `cpType`, with the jointness in `joint` / `jointCpCategory` — so the sheet treated it as an ordinary CP and demanded a terminal status the parent must not reach yet.
- Fix: new `CpVisitDetail.isJointCpVisit()` (participants OR jointCpCategory OR normalised cpType) in `CpOutcomeContract.kt`; the sheet records it when the detail loads (`detailSaysJointCp`) and ORs it into `isJointCp`. `contractValue()` now also normalises spaces. `TripNavigationFragment.isJointCpWorkflow()` had a weaker unnormalised check and now shares `isJointCpTypeValue`.
- `:app:compileDebugKotlin` clean, `:app:testDebugUnitTest` BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Not yet exercised against a real joint CP on a device.

## 2026-09-23 — Stale PERMISSION_MISSING alerts now clear themselves
- Backend clears PERMISSION_MISSING / GPS_DISABLED / LOCATION_DISABLED only on a heartbeat carrying `locationEnabled = true` (postgres_repository.go:601). Heartbeats came only from the tracking service, which runs only clock-in → clock-out, so a staffer who granted the permission outside a shift kept the alert until their NEXT clock-in and the live board showed an already-fixed problem.
- `GeoTrackBootstrapSync.queuePermissionHealth` used to `return` when nothing was missing. It now calls `queuePermissionCleared`, which enqueues one HEARTBEAT event with `locationEnabled = true`.

- All-device safety: no new permissions; `isDeviceLocationEnabled` already branches for API < 28; existing Q/TIRAMISU guards untouched; `batteryPct` nullable so it is simply omitted when unknown. Uses the existing HEARTBEAT queue type and endpoint — no backend change needed.

## 2026-09-23 — iOS login: OTP field dead after app switch, and card overflow
- OTP unresponsive after leaving to copy the code: iOS resigns first responder when the app backgrounds, but `focusedOtpBox` still pointed at the same box, so SwiftUI saw NO state change, `OtpTextField.updateUIView` never ran and `becomeFirstResponder()` was never re-issued. Tapping that same box assigned the identical value — also not a change — so tapping did nothing, however many times. (Tapping a DIFFERENT box would have worked; that matches the reported symptom.)
- Fix: `refocusOtp(at:)` clears `focusedOtpBox` then reassigns on the next runloop, forcing the transition. Called from `.onAppear`, from `.onChange(of: scenePhase)` when active (the return from Messages), and from a box tap.
- Card overflow: the sheet background was painted into a FIXED rect — `sheetHeight(geo) + 60`, a fraction of screen height — not the card own bounds, so taller content (keyboard up / large text) spilled below the white area and the Employee ID button hung on the dark backdrop. Now a `RoundedRectangle` filling the real bounds with `.padding(.bottom, -60)` to keep the lower corners off-screen; added `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: sheetHeight(geo), alignment: .top)` to preserve the full width and the designed proportion the fixed rect used to supply.

## 2026-09-23 — GeoTrack stop-gap investigation: measured, and the assumed cause is wrong
- No SSH to .179 from this machine (host unresolvable, IP times out), so prod SQL was unavailable; evidence is code + the live geo API via the user's browser session.
- DECISIVE PROBE against prod `/api/geotrack/timeline` (24h window, admin token): 4 staff with live coords and lastSeen 0 min -> 0 points; a BOGUS staffId -> 0 points, HTTP 200, NO error; staffId omitted entirely -> 0 points. All three identical. A honoured `staffId` would have errored on the bogus id ("does not match any employee"). So the parameter is discarded and the query runs for the CALLER. `/api/geotrack/timeline` is pinned to the caller in prod, confirmed empirically.
- This corrects the teammate's report: the live page is NOT deriving "a fraction" of the 2,077 stored stops because point density is thin. It receives ZERO points for anyone but the viewer, so it derives ZERO stops. Density is not the cause.
- It also reorders their plan: switching the page to `/api/geotrack/session-route` (their item 2) would NOT help, because session-route resolves staff through the same pinned `resolveStaffID` (server.go:743). Viewer scope is the single blocker on items 1 AND 2, not just item 1.
- Algorithm differences found (secondary, only matter once data flows): browser `buildSegments` clusters stationary segments within 50 m and emits a stop at >=30 s, ignoring `speed` entirely; service `computeStops` treats `movement_mode=='stationary' OR speed<0.5` as stationary, 50 m from a running centroid, and requires >=3 min. The service also only stores stops INSIDE trips (`summarizeTrip(staffID,start,end)`, `trip_stops` keyed by trip_id), so stationary time outside a trip is never stored.
- FIX APPLIED (web repo, branch `dev`, pulled per user instruction): `convex/http.ts` `/api/auth/geotrack-access` now also returns `scope: canViewLive ? "all" : "self"`, reusing the already-computed and cached `canViewLive` (= isAdmin || attendance.liveTracking) rather than inventing a second permission notion. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. NOT DEPLOYED — never-deploy-convex stands.

## 2026-09-23 — Why 190 sessions but only ~52 sending points
- STRUCTURAL CAUSE, confirmed in code: `GeoTrackBootstrapSync.sync()` creates the server-side session via `startDirectTracking` gated only on `geoConsentGiven` (L69) and an open attendance session. `queuePermissionHealth` (L75) only REPORTS missing permissions — it never blocks. So a session is opened for every consented, clocked-in staffer regardless of whether the phone can produce a fix. "Sessions" therefore counts clock-ins, not working tracking; part of the 190 vs 52 gap is definitional, not a failure.

  - 28 of the stale rows are at battery <=5%.
  - `isNetworkAvailable=false` on 150/150 stale rows. NOT usable as evidence: verified on origin/main that neither the missed-heartbeat job nor the web repo writes that column any more (only an explicit NETWORK_OFFLINE does, postgres_web_repository.go:265), and the column is sticky — a silent phone keeps whatever was last written, possibly from before that fix deployed. Fresh rows show 6 true / 4 false.

- Second handset (CPH2363) is a **sideloaded v87 test unit** (`installerPackageName=pc`), all permissions granted, battery-whitelisted, and its `geotrack_permission_alert` channel DOES exist — so the alert mechanism works when the guards pass. - Ruled out stationary throttling with the constants, not by assumption: `HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS = 75_000` and the heartbeat carries no GPS, so a live service pings every 75 s regardless of movement or location permission. `STATIONARY_PING_INTERVAL_MS = 5 min` throttles stored POINTS only. Server `is_online` is a stored column refreshed by heartbeat and flipped by the 15-min missed-heartbeat job (`DefaultHeartbeatMissedAfter`). **The board is telling the truth** — those phones' services really are dead.
- **Defect found and fixed** (different symptom, real): `allGranted()` accepted fine-OR-coarse while `missingPermissionKeys()` requires precise. A coarse-only phone therefore: (a) never saw the gate, so was never asked to upgrade; (b) still got the ongoing red alert for `fine_location`; (c) tapping that alert re-checks `allGranted`, finds true, and declines to open the gate — **a permanent, unfixable red notification**; and (d) per the existing note on `hasPreciseLocation`, ~2 km fixes fail the 50 m capture gate, so it saves no GPS — "Live with a frozen pin". Aligned 4 call sites (`allGranted`, the Location row's click, `refreshStatus`'s switch, `openDeviceLocationSettings`) to `hasPreciseLocation`; deliberately left the 2 background-location **prerequisite** checks on fine-OR-coarse, since Android grants "all the time" on top of either. `TrackingPermissionSetup.requestRuntime` already re-requests FINE, so the gate can actually heal it.
- Note this fixes "online but frozen pin", NOT the 93 offline phones — different symptom, stated as such rather than conflated.
- **Could not determine why the 93 died.** No fleet-wide tamper-reason endpoint exists: `day-status` is a list but returns no reason codes (44 rows, same shape as live-status), and `timeline` is per-staff and still caller-pinned on prod. The pending Convex `scope` field (written, on dev) is the unblocker for that. Did not invent web/geo edits — found no defect on either side today; the board is accurate.

Historical shape from that August window is still informative: GPS_DISABLED 484, LOCATION_DISABLED 322, PERMISSION_MISSING 177 vs DEVICE_REBOOT 34 / DEVICE_SHUTDOWN 5 / APP_UPDATED 9 — i.e. permission/GPS problems dominated, NOT OEM process kills.
- **The decisive measurement** (12:30 IST, 220 phones with `tracking_active`): split by `updated_at` vs `last_seen` —
  - `bothFresh` (genuinely online): **27**
  - **`rowFreshSeenStale`: 152** — row written inside 15 min, `last_seen` stale
  - `bothStale`: 41
  - median `last_seen − updated_at` gap: **193 minutes**
- So the phones are **not dead**. 152 of them are awake, online, and talking to the server — the row keeps being refreshed — while no heartbeat or location arrives. `SyncSession` bumps `updated_at` and `tracking_active` but never touches `last_seen`; only a heartbeat/fix does. Corroborated by the 11:01→12:28 bucket arithmetic: the 1–4 h bucket stayed ~100 instead of ageing into 4–12 h (which grew by only 10), so it is being continuously refilled, not draining.

- **This exposed a real hole in `dea4b4c4`, which I pushed this morning.** `sync()` returns `session.shouldTrackNow`, and `applyDirectSession` sets that purely from "a server session exists" — it starts the service only if permissions allow, but returns true either way. So `if (!started) reconcilePermissionAlert(...)` never fired on precisely the 152-phone majority. Corrected to `if (!GeoTrackService.isRunning)`. Safe unconditionally because `update()` clears the alert when nothing is missing.

## 2026-09-24 — The silent failure that stops capture: FGS start refused in the background
- `GeoTrackService.start()` ends in `runCatching { startForegroundService(intent) }.onFailure { Log.e(...) }`. **The exception was logged and otherwise swallowed** — nothing on the device or the server learned that capture never began. `grep` confirms `ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException` is handled nowhere in the app.
- Android 12+ (API 31+; app targets 36) refuses `startForegroundService()` from the background unless the app is exempt — the battery-optimisation allowlist being the exemption that applies here. `TrackingCheckWorker` runs **in the background every 15 minutes** and reaches `start()` via `sync()` → `applyDirectSession()`. On a non-exempt phone that call throws every single time.
- This matches the production measurement exactly: the session sync immediately before it SUCCEEDS (so `updated_at` and `tracking_active` advance), then the service start throws (so no heartbeat, no fix, `last_seen` frozen). 152 of 220 phones, median `last_seen` 3.2 h stale.
- Ruled out first, so this is not a guess by elimination: `hasRequiredLocationPermissions()` requires only fine-OR-coarse plus `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION` — it does **not** demand background location, so it is not over-gating. Manifest declares `foregroundServiceType="location"` and both FGS permissions correctly.
- **Fix:** `start()` now logs the exception CLASS and raises the ongoing permission alert, which names `battery_optimization` — the setting that actually lifts the restriction. `update()` self-clears, so it cannot stick.
- **Honest limits.** This is a strong hypothesis, not yet proven on the fleet: neither connected handset can test it (the user's has no location permission at all, so `start()` returns before the throw; the other is battery-whitelisted, so it would succeed). Once v90 ships, the log line names the exception and the alert makes it visible, which converts the hypothesis into a measurement.
- **What the app cannot do:** Android does not let an app exempt itself from battery optimisation. The app can ask; the staff member must accept. A code-only path exists (expedited WorkManager + `setForeground()`, which is permitted from background) but it is a second capture path through the highest-risk code in the repo — not taken without the user's say-so.
- compileDebugKotlin + testDebugUnitTest green; prod hosts; versionCode 90.

## 2026-09-24 — Expedited revival worker, one permission list, every missing permission shown — verified on device
- **Revival worker** (`TrackingRevivalWorker`, new): when the watchdog finds the service not running but permissions present, it enqueues an expedited one-shot worker that takes its own foreground slot via `setForeground()` and starts `GeoTrackService` underneath it — the one Android 12+ exemption the app can reach itself ("an app that already has a foreground service may start another"). Separate one-shot because `setExpedited` does not exist on periodic work. Distinct notification id 9003 so tearing the worker down cannot demote the service. `RUN_AS_NON_EXPEDITED_WORK_REQUEST` so exhausted quota still gets an attempt.
- **Manifest:** WorkManager's `SystemForegroundService` was declared with NO `foregroundServiceType`; a location-typed `ForegroundInfo` would throw `MissingForegroundServiceTypeException` on Android 14+. Merged `foregroundServiceType="location"` in via `tools:node="merge"`.
- **One permission list.** The same conditions were hand-written in FOUR places (gate, bootstrap sync, twice in `GeoTrackService`) and had drifted — that drift is what caused the coarse-location trap. The service now defers to `missingPermissionKeys()`, and `allGranted()` is DEFINED as `missingPermissionKeys().isEmpty()`, so the gate and alert can no longer disagree.
- **Two keys added**, both previously silent: `location_services` (with GPS off `missing` was empty, so the alert CLEARED ITSELF) and `notification` (whose absence stops the alert being posted at all). New Notifications row in the gate with its own allow action; labels added.

Checked instead, on the built APK with aapt2: WorkManager service `foregroundServiceType=0x8` (location) ✅, `GeoTrackService` still `0x8` ✅, `rowNotifications`/`switchNotifications` compiled in ✅. Allowlist restored and location confirmed on afterwards.

Proposed decoupling: let the app-version endpoint honour the minimum while the login guard stays off; then set the minimum to 90 only after v90 is live on Play.

(iOS does have the equivalent — `AppUpdateCoordinator.swift` — so platform coverage was not the blocker.) Updates stay manual / Play auto-update.

## 2026-09-25 — iOS users not Online on the web board (root cause + fix, local)
- Could not read `/api/geotrack/live-status` (needs the user's web session; the only connected browser is the Mac admin PC, which is off-limits), so this is from code. Board rule (geo service `postgres_repository.go`): Online = `is_online AND last_seen >= now() - 5 min`; a healthy phone heartbeats every 75 s.
- **Root cause (iOS only):** `LocationManager.swift` set `pausesLocationUpdatesAutomatically = true` (since `cffade02`, 2026-03-22, shipped in every M-Chat build incl. 54). Once the person stops moving iOS pauses the location session → the app is suspended → the heartbeat Task stops → Offline after 5 min, and it stays Offline until the app is next opened because a paused session is only restarted by the app. Android is immune (foreground service + alarm heartbeat). No handler for `locationManagerDidPauseLocationUpdates` existed either.
- **Fix, FoundationChat `darx`, LOCAL only (asked before push):** `pausesLocationUpdatesAutomatically = false` + `locationManagerDidPauseLocationUpdates` restarts updates while still awake; build bumped to 55. Not compiled (no Mac). Battery bounded by the existing 100 m background filter/accuracy.

## 2026-09-26 — How SV approval works on iOS (read-only trace)
- Two approval paths, both driven by the backend, none by a dedicated "approve SV" screen: (1) **Same-area / CP-routed SV** — the field staffer completes the linked CP visit in `CompleteCpVisitSheet` (locked-SV mode: chooser → "Site Visit" → "Confirm Site Visit"), which calls `setCpVisitOutcome(outcome: "converted_to_site_visit")`; the backend hook in `clientPlaceVisits.ts` (~9482) flips the linked `siteVisits` row `confirmationStatus: pending → confirmed`, `confirmationRequiredBy: "cp"`, `confirmedByStaffId = visit.assignedStaffId`. "Reject SV" → `rejectCpVisitOutcome(outcome: "rejected", notes)` marks the SV rejected; "Cancel SV" → `cancelCpVisit`. (2) **Out-of-station / immediate-pickup SV** — creation returns a `handoffId`, not an SV; the GM gets an `out_of_station_handoff` daily task and approves from **Tasks → Complete** (`POST /api/dailyTasks/updateStatus {status: "completed"}`), which `dailyTasks.ts` (~3411) routes into `internalConfirmHandoffAsSv` (mints the real SV, sends svconfirmation, fans out telecaller + Site Incharge tasks); **Cancel** cancels the handoff. Authorised: the assigned GM, super-admins, or `marketing.siteVisits.confirm`. The dedicated `/api/marketing/outOfStationHandoffs/confirm` route exists but neither app calls it. Android mirrors both paths (`CompleteCpVisitBottomSheet.onLockedConfirmTap`, `TaskManagerFragment` handoff actions).
